p.src: Overview: Hamilton’s equations do more than repackage the equations of motion. They define a velocity field on phase space whose divergence vanishes. That simple cancellation is Liouville’s theorem: Hamiltonian evolution preserves phase-space volume. We shall reach it in the order in which its meaning becomes visible—first energy conservation, then constant-energy surfaces, then a fluid of possible initial conditions, and finally the contrast between volume-preserving flow and a dissipative sink. The same language leads naturally to Poisson brackets.

ja: 概観: ハミルトンの方程式は運動方程式を単に書き換える以上のことをする。それらは相空間上の速度場を定義し、その発散はゼロである。この単純な相殺がリウヴィルの定理である。すなわち、ハミルトン的発展は相空間の体積を保存する。その意味が見えてくる順序でこれに到達しよう—まずエネルギー保存、次に等エネルギー面、次に可能な初期条件の流体、そして最後に体積保存流と散逸的吸い込みの対比である。同じ言語が自然にポアソン括弧へと導く。
zh: 概述: 哈密顿方程所做的远不止重新包装运动方程。它们在相空间上定义了一个散度为零的速度场。这一简单的相消就是刘维尔定理：哈密顿演化保持相空间体积。我们将按照其含义逐渐显现的顺序来达到它—首先是能量守恒，然后是等能面，接着是可能初始条件构成的流体，最后是保体积流与耗散汇之间的对比。同样的语言自然地引向泊松括号。

In a reversible discrete law, every state has one arrow entering and one arrow leaving. The present is enough to determine both the next state and the preceding one. A bad law sends many states into one sink: the future may be determined, but the past is no longer recoverable.

ja: 我々が求める定理は、講義の冒頭で導入した可逆な状態図の連続的古典対応物である。可逆な離散法則では、各状態には入る矢印が一つと出る矢印が一つある。現在は次の状態と前の状態の両方を決定するのに十分である。悪い法則は多くの状態を一つの吸い込みへ送る。未来は決定されても、過去はもはや回復できない。
zh: 我们要寻求的定理，是课程开头引入的可逆状态图的连续经典对应物。在可逆的离散定律中，每个状态都有一条箭头进入、一条箭头离开。现在足以确定下一个状态和先前的状态。坏的定律把许多状态送入一个汇：未来或许可以确定，但过去不再可恢复。

p.src: Liouville’s theorem says what becomes of that distinction when the set of states is a continuous phase space. The phrase replacing one arrow in and one arrow out will be as much flow in as flow out. Before that phrase can be made mathematical, however, we need to reconstruct the flow from Hamilton’s equations.

p.src: There is a historical puzzle in doing so. Hamilton, Jacobi, Lagrange, and Poisson built elaborate and beautiful forms of classical mechanics without knowing the quantum theory in which those forms would become indispensable. Newton had a direct target: planetary motion. Lagrange and Hamilton also had physical problems before them, but they pursued analogies and structures far beyond any one orbit. Stationary action in mechanics resembled least-time principles in optics; ray motion and particle motion could be put into parallel mathematical forms. They simplified, rearranged, and unified the equations because the structures themselves appeared to contain physics.

ja: そうすることには歴史的な謎がある。ハミルトン、ヤコビ、ラグランジュ、ポアソンは、それらの形式が不可欠となる量子論を知らずに、精巧で美しい古典力学の形式を築いた。ニュートンには直接の目標があった。惑星運動である。ラグランジュとハミルトンも目の前に物理的問題を持っていたが、彼らは一つの軌道をはるかに超えた類似と構造を追求した。力学における停留作用は光学における最小時間原理に似ていた。光線の運動と粒子の運動は平行な数学的形式に置くことができた。構造自体が物理学を含んでいるように見えたので、彼らは方程式を単純化し、並べ替え、統一した。
zh: 这样做有一个历史谜题。哈密顿、雅可比、拉格朗日和泊松构建了精巧而优美的经典力学形式，却并不知道量子理论会使这些形式变得不可或缺。牛顿有一个直接的目标：行星运动。拉格朗日和哈密顿面前也有物理问题，但他们追求的类比和结构远远超出任何单一轨道。力学中的稳定作用量类似于光学中的最短时间原理；光线运动和粒子运动可以被纳入平行的数学形式。他们简化、重新排列并统一了方程，因为这些结构本身似乎就包含着物理。

p.src: We now know that this instinct was extraordinarily productive. Logically, many features of classical mechanics can be understood as limits of quantum mechanics. Historically, the order was reversed: the classical structures were found first, and only much later did their deeper use become clear. A provocative joke attributed to Feynman made the point by contrasting mathematics pursued internally with physics constrained by an external partner, the physical world. The joke is not an argument, but the distinction is useful: formal beauty matters here because nature repeatedly selects these formal structures.

p.src:
Let a system have $n$ canonical pairs, $(q_i,p_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.$ There is one momentum for each coordinate and one coordinate for each momentum. The law of motion is packaged in one function, $H=H(q_1,\ldots,q_n,p_1,\ldots,p_n,t),$ and Hamilton’s equations are $\boxed{
  \dot q_i=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i},
  \qquad
  \dot p_i=-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q_i}.}$ The sign is part of the canonical structure. The $q$-equation carries the plus sign; the $p$-equation carries the minus sign.

p.src: Response: Hamilton’s equations define the formal theory once $H(q,p)$ and the canonical pairs are specified. There is no universal extra assumption $p=m\dot q$. That relation holds for an ordinary Cartesian particle with quadratic kinetic energy, but other coordinates and other Hamiltonians give other momentum–velocity relations. p.src:
If a canonical transformation expands a range of positions by a factor $a$, the conjugate momentum scale contracts by the reciprocal factor: $q\longrightarrow aq,
  \qquad
  p\longrightarrow \frac{p}{a},
  \qquad
  dq\,dp\longrightarrow dq\,dp.$ This is the clean phase-space content behind the gas-expansion example. In an adiabatic expansion, the accessible ordinary-space region grows while typical momenta fall and the gas cools. A detailed thermodynamic relation depends on dimension, the expansion protocol, and interactions; Liouville’s theorem supplies the volume constraint, not every thermodynamic coefficient.

p.src: Response: Liouville’s theorem applies whenever the complete dynamics is Hamiltonian, including explicitly time-dependent canonical variables. Expansion in position directions must be accompanied by the corresponding contraction in canonical-momentum directions. A cosmological scale factor, a controlled expansion of a gas, and a freely exploding cloud are not the same physical process, however. A Hubble-like correlation between distance and recession speed can arise because faster objects travel farther, whereas adiabatic cooling concerns contraction of the local momentum distribution. The theorem constrains the full phase-space map in either case.

p.src: Response: For any finite time the ideal differential equation still has an inverse, so exact data can be run backward. The precise statement is that finite phase-space cells contract exponentially. Recovering their past then requires exponentially increasing precision, and at infinite time all trajectories approach the sink. This is the closest continuous classical analogue of the discrete loss-of-alternatives picture, not an assertion that two exact finite-time solutions literally become one.

ja: これが、一つの矢印が入り一つの矢印が出るという事柄の連続版である。形は変わりうるし、角度も変わりうるし、隣接する軌道は甚だしく離れうる。滑らかで閉じたハミルトニアンの記述において起こりえないのは、有限個の選択肢の集まりがより小さな相空間体積へと圧縮されることである。$H=pq$の流れは引き伸ばす自由を示し、縮約された減衰振動子はハミルトニアンの条件が放棄されると現れる吸い込み口を示す。そしてポアソン括弧は、同じ力学を、ハミルトニアンがすべての時間微分を生成するという命題へと凝縮する。
zh: 这就是一进一出的连续版本。形状可以改变，角度可以改变，相邻轨迹可以极其剧烈地分离。在光滑闭合的哈密顿描述中不可能发生的是，把有限多个备选状态压缩进更小的相空间体积。$H=pq$流展示了拉伸的自由；约化阻尼振子展示了一旦放弃哈密顿条件就出现的汇。随后，泊松括号把同一动力学浓缩为这样一个陈述：哈密顿量生成每一个时间导数。
